Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

stablr 0.3.0.9000 (development)

Fixes

  • Compiled-boundary fail-closed validation (Phase 13 PR-1). elnet.fit now length-validates the sparse standardization attributes and rejects non-finite xs before .Call (previously a missing/short attribute reached the compiled engine and read out of bounds), rejects NA in x (dense and stored sparse entries), y, and weights with an informative error (previously affected columns were dropped silently), and warns at the boundary with code-specific messages before returning list(jerr=...) on non-fatal codes. Behavior on well-formed inputs is unchanged.
  • RNG hygiene (Phase 13 PR-2). stabl_fit() no longer permanently clobbers the global RNG: .Random.seed is saved on entry and restored on exit, so later unseeded randomness in the caller’s session is no longer a deterministic function of the last random_state. Nested CV results no longer depend on cv_workers (per-fold seeds are drawn before workers fork), and all multi-omic fan-out sites (per-fold, per-omic, early/late/cooperative fusion, downstream predictors) derive independent RNG streams instead of reusing one random_state. Two downstream cv.glmnet fits that drew their internal fold assignment from the ambient stream are now seeded. Multi-omic numerical outputs under explicit seeds change accordingly (per-omic feature selections are unchanged); the Python-parity contract for the core STABL algorithm is unaffected and its fixtures pass byte-identically.

Documentation

  • All nine vignettes audited against the current API and re-rendered. Replaced 25 deprecated get_feature_names_out() calls with get_feature_names(), jaccard_matrix() with jaccard_similarity_matrix(), adjusted_similarity(nb_total_elements=) with n_universe=, and deprecated groups= arguments to stabl_fit() with sample_groups= (advanced, environments). Corrected the stabl_multiomic_train_validate() group argument to groups_train (multiomic, cooperative) and the stale groups note in the environments vignette.
  • Added seven figure chunks so key conclusions are visually supported: environment-wise minimum-score heatmap (environments), Cox stability path, Jaccard similarity heatmap and interpretation scatter (advanced), late-fusion prediction scatter (multiomic), cooperative rho surface (cooperative), and FDR+ regularisation curve (intro).
  • Advanced vignette: the grouped-bootstrap and reproducibility examples now pass hard_threshold = 0.5 so the demonstration selects a non-empty set at p = 10 (the default data-driven threshold legitimately selects nothing there, which made the Jaccard comparison vacuous); the Cox example text now states that the FDR threshold saturates at 1, so the selection set is empty and the planted features are recovered in the importances ranking and the sparse end of the stability path.
  • Multiomic vignette: the late-fusion scatter is accompanied by an honest note that the compact build settings (10 bootstraps, 6-lambda grids) demonstrate workflow shape, not competitive prediction.
  • Intro vignette: section 7.3 benchmark table replaced with the current learner-benchmark calibration ratios (benchmarks/learner_comparison/), and next-steps pointers added to the getting-started vignette and the sPLS-DA / random-forest material.
  • Getting-started vignette: corrected the knockoff_equi “Why” table cell – decoys are conservative for tree learners, and measured calibration is learner- and regime-dependent (see the pairing table in vignette("stablr-intro")).
  • sPLS-DA coverage extended: new section in the advanced vignette (multinomial data via the binomial adapter), topic-table row, a bullet in the TCGA learner notes, and an adapter pointer in the cooperative DIABLO paragraph.

New features

  • New experimental base learner base_learner = "splsda": sparse PLS discriminant analysis via mixOmics for binary classification (family = "binomial" only). The STABL lambda grid sweeps sPLS-DA’s per-component keepX; a feature counts as selected when any retained component loading exceeds splsda_ncomp-independent magnitude 1e-10. New exports: make_splsda_adapter() (standalone adapter factory, mirroring make_glmnet_adapter()) and auto_splsda_keepx_grid() (geometric keepX grid used by lambda_grid = "auto"), plus the stabl_fit(splsda_ncomp = 2L) argument. Empirical calibration on a multi-cohort benchmark (benchmarks/mint_comparison/): sPLS-DA + random permutation was the best-calibrated configuration (FDP/FDP+ ratio 1.01); knockoff pairings should be validated per dataset.

stablr 0.3.0

Maturity benchmarks

  • Interpretation/validated-workflow benchmark committed (IV, 110 runs, predeclared gates): effect-direction recovery 1.00, null validated AUROC centred at chance (median 0.473), leaky full-data selection directionally optimistic over nested (+0.015 mean AUROC), one-feature folds non-degenerate. Redundancy co-selection gate NOT met (0.60): correlated substitutes are always grouped when co-selected (10/10), but FDP+ selection prunes members in 4/10 seeds. Adverse result committed (benchmarks/iv_summary.md; Gate B report in docs/plans/).

  • Ordinal regression learner (base_learner = "ordinal", ordinalNet proportional-odds): simulated calibration (10 seeds x 2 designs) gives knockoff_equi mean FDP+ 0.00 (nominal 0.1) but mean TPR 0.37 – strongly conservative; graduation bar (FDP+ <= 0.15, TPR >= 0.8) NOT met, so the learner stays experimental (benchmarks/ws9_summary.md). (simulation evidence; summaries in benchmarks/)

  • Random-forest adapter graduated within a measured scope (WS-2, 60 runs): rf + knockoff_equi meets the predeclared criterion (mean FDP <= 0.15, TPR >= 0.8) on linear and low-dimensional nonlinear designs; NOT met at p = 50 with strong correlation or for binary outcomes. Man pages and the pkgdown section document the scope.

  • Oblique random-forest adapter fenced (WS-3, 40 runs): no predeclared remedy reached the criterion; knockoff decoy importance is inflated. Man pages recommend base_learner = “rf” for knockoff-calibrated selection.

  • Cooperative-fusion benchmark committed (WS-4, 60 runs): no fusion mode dominates; cooperative fusion is competitive; the late-fusion gaussian weakness is documented as a caveat. Cox cooperative fusion is permanently deferred (no CV-loss precedent; fail-closed stops guard the engine).

  • Environment-stability workflow promoted with a documented scope (WS-5, 60 runs): min-aggregation controls FDP+ across location-shift and prevalence-drift designs; per-environment permutation rows are documented anti-conservative.

  • Knockoff high-dimensional boundary recorded as permanent (WS-7 decision record, docs/plans/).

  • Learner-regime guidance table shipped in the intro vignette, section 7.3 (WS-6).

  • plot_stabl_path now draws the path in canonical decreasing-lambda order regardless of grid row order, aligns artificial-feature lines to the same order, and shows x-axis tick labels.

Release governance

  • SCI-04 null-selected-fraction gate accepted on 2026-10-16 by the project owner acting in the reviewer role (accepted record SCI-04-null-selected-fraction-v2-accepted, reviewer response in inst/analysis/review/). This is a provisional owner acceptance: the review packet’s itemized independent confirmation remains outstanding. The release contract pins the Hoeffding criterion (alpha = 0.05, U <= 0.10, n = 150 replicates) and the methodology validation now evaluates the bound per null cell instead of failing closed. Remaining release blockers: the fresh full-candidate run at the accepted replicate count and the independent confirmation.
  • IV-benchmark CI smoke workflow (weekly schedule + manual dispatch) runs the interpretation/validation benchmark end-to-end at shrunken settings and asserts run completeness.

Documentation

  • Documentation website restyled after the dreamlet site (Flatly theme, KaTeX math rendering, maintainer links on the authors page); the pkgdown workflow now deploys the site on every push to main.
  • Homepage restructured to lead with resources, motivation, the analysis workflow diagram, and installation; release-governance detail moved to docs/RELEASE_STATUS.md.
  • All eight vignettes rewritten in the formal register of the limma User’s Guide (numbered task-oriented sections, declarative prose, output interpretation); code chunks are unchanged.
  • inst/CITATION derives the package version dynamically instead of hardcoding it.
  • pkgdown reference index extended with the knockoff feature constructors.

Cross-study reliability: study-disjoint resampling (B1–B3)

  • New study_labels argument on stabl_multiomic_nested_cv() declares the sampling unit of the cross-validation. When supplied (a named vector covering exactly the sample IDs), whole studies become the CV unit: outer folds assign whole studies (outer_v equal to the number of studies gives leave-one-study-out), inner candidate-selection folds are study-disjoint within each outer training split, and stratified = TRUE is reinterpreted at the study level through a deterministic largest-first greedy pass that minimises class-proportion imbalance. The default study_labels = NULL preserves the sample-i.i.d. scheme byte-identically (fold_scheme = "sample_iid"). Study disjointness concerns the CV folds only — bootstrap_strata (sampling design) and SGL feature_groups (features) remain orthogonal.
  • Fail-closed validation for the study-disjoint scheme: label names must cover exactly the sample IDs; at least max(outer_v, 2) studies; each outer-training split needs at least inner_v + 1 studies; every validation fold (outer and inner) must hold both outcome classes; and 1-sample studies are rejected. stabl_multiomic_nested_cv() also gained a majority-class fallback when a fold’s selection leaves fewer than two features (previously a glmnet error).
  • Provenance and reporting: the nested-CV object records fold_scheme ("sample_iid" / "study_disjoint") and the validated study_labels; under the study-disjoint scheme each fold carries study_ids and held-out class_counts, and print() shows the scheme.
  • New stabl_multiomic_study_diagnostics() (inferred scope, flagged): per-study outcome composition and per-feature absolute standardized mean differences versus the pooled rest, quantifying the study-level shift that motivates study-disjoint folds.
  • New stabl_multiomic_study_split() (inferred scope, flagged): a deterministic study-disjoint train/validation split (greedy, seeded, class-balanced) feeding stabl_multiomic_train_validate(). stabl_multiomic_cv() already supports group-disjoint assessment folds through its groups argument and now records fold_scheme = "group_disjoint" for provenance.
  • Benchmark evidence: benchmarks/b1_study_disjoint_cv.R compares held-out BER under sample-i.i.d. versus study-disjoint outer folds on multi-study simulations, isolating two batch mechanisms: class-independent location shifts on null features (a deliberate null probe — the gap is approximately zero there, as expected) and outcome-prevalence drift across studies (gap ≈ +0.04 BER over 10 seeds, positive in 9 of 10 seeds — the sample-i.i.d. estimate is optimistic precisely when study-level outcome composition differs). Per-fold selection sets are persisted (b1_selected_features.csv) for the Round C stability-of-stability analysis.

Cross-study reliability: reporting, comparison, and guardrails (C1–C5)

All Round C items are inferred scope (the approved plan flags them for audit reconciliation):

  • Per-study performance (C1): stabl_multiomic_nested_cv() now returns performance_by_study when study_labels is supplied — per-study outer held-out accuracy and balanced error rate pooled across folds and repeats (NA balanced error rate for studies whose pooled held-out predictions contain a single outcome class). NULL under the sample-i.i.d. scheme.
  • Scheme comparison helper (C2): new stabl_multiomic_scheme_comparison() runs the same nested CV under both sampling units (sample-i.i.d. and study-disjoint) with matched arguments and returns both objects plus a comparison table and the BER gap (positive = the sample-i.i.d. estimate was optimistic).
  • Harmonization guardrail (C3, documentation): the CV docs now warn that batch harmonization (e.g. ComBat) fitted on the full dataset before cross-validation leaks study-level information across folds; fit harmonization within training folds or interpret metrics as conditional on that step. Study-disjoint folds do not repair leakage from pooled preprocessing.
  • Stability of stability (C4): new stabl_multiomic_selection_stability() computes fold x fold Jaccard similarity of the selected feature sets across the outer folds of a study-disjoint nested CV (the deferred selection-stability heatmap analysis; render with stats::heatmap()).
  • Grouped-CV guardrail (C5): stabl_multiomic_cv() now fails closed when a grouped assessment fold holds a single outcome class under a classification family (mirroring the study-disjoint validation); regression is unaffected.

Two-tier API: beginner stabl() + expert stabl_fit()

  • New stabl(): a one-stop-shop entry point for first-time and application users. Pass a data.frame (or a matrix plus an outcome vector; the outcome may also be named as a column of the data.frame) and it runs STABL with statistically safe defaults — model-X knockoff artificial features (artificial_type = "knockoff_equi"), FDP+ calibration, strict knockoff fallback (knockoff_fallback = "stop"), and an automatic lambda grid. Roughly eight arguments cover the common cases; everything else is forwarded to stabl_fit() through ....
  • New S3 methods for the stabl class: print.stabl() (plain-language answer: what was fitted, which features were selected, the achieved FDP+ estimate), summary.stabl(), and plot.stabl() (stability paths plus the FDP+ curve). stabl objects also remain full stabl_fit objects, so every accessor and workflow applies unchanged.
  • New beginner generics support() and feature_names() with methods for stabl and stabl_fit; they delegate to get_support() and get_feature_names().

Renamed functions and arguments (old names kept as deprecation shims)

Each old name still works: it warns once per session and delegates to the new name. Positional calls are unaffected.

Old name New name Why
stabl_fit(groups =) stabl_fit(sample_groups =) groups collided with feature_groups; sample- vs feature-grouping is now unambiguous
get_feature_names_out() get_feature_names() drops the sklearn-ism; reads naturally in R
stacked_multi_omic() stabl_multiomic_stacked() joins the stabl_multiomic_* family and fixes the multi_omic/multiomic casing split
jaccard_matrix() jaccard_similarity_matrix() states what the matrix contains
adjusted_similarity_values() adjusted_similarity_pairwise() the triplet now reads pair / all-pairs matrix / summary consistently
adjusted_similarity_measure() adjusted_similarity_summary() as above
pearson_similarity_values() pearson_similarity_pairwise() as above
pearson_similarity_measure() pearson_similarity_summary() as above
classic_bootstrap_indices() sample_bootstrap_indices() states what is resampled (samples, not features or groups)
pearson_similarity_pairwise(d =) / _summary(d =) nb_total_elements = aligns the element-count argument with the adjusted-similarity family (d = still accepted with a deprecation warning)

Documentation

  • pkgdown reference index reorganized into tiers: Getting started, Core, Workflows, Expert, Metrics, Plotting, Data, and a dedicated Deprecated section.
  • New vignette “Getting started with stabl” — a beginner walkthrough from a data.frame to a plain-language selection.
  • README gains a two-tier quick start (beginner stabl() first, expert stabl_fit() second).
  • All help pages regenerated; every shim’s help page points to its replacement.

stablr 0.2.2

Scientific hardening (audit A1-A3, E1-E3)

  • Strict fallback policy (flagged behavior change): when a knockoff constructor fails on a supported-dimensional input, the previous behavior was to warn and silently fall back to random-permutation features — which do not support FDP+ calibration, so the fit’s FDP+ estimates silently changed target. make_artificial_features() and stabl_fit() now take knockoff_fallback = "stop" (the default): the fallback is an error with an actionable message. knockoff_fallback = "allow" restores the warn-and-fall-back behavior (recorded in the provenance fallback_history). The benign knockoff_mvr -> knockoff_equi fallback is unaffected (both are model-X constructions with valid FDP+ calibration) and remains a warning under either policy. Related fix: the linear-algebra infeasibility classifier now recognizes the hyphenated “not positive-definite” and “cannot solve SDP” messages emitted by the knockoff package’s SDP solver, so those failures are typed and handled consistently instead of escaping as raw errors.
  • RF/oblique-RF confirmatory guard extended: the runtime guardrail for multivariate RF learners now also fires for the fixed-X knockoff pairing (fixed-X exchangeability does not survive bootstrap row subsampling), not only for random_permutation. The model-X pairings (knockoff_equi, knockoff_mvr) remain warning-free.
  • Covariance terminology: the fixed-X knockoff documentation now states the actual contract (second-moment/Gram structure on the input scale) rather than “covariance structure”.
  • SCI-04 feasibility clause (E1): the draft SCI-04-null-selected-fraction-v2 contract now documents that the proposed release criterion U <= 0.10 (Hoeffding, alpha = 0.05) is vacuous at the previously considered n = 100 replicates (margin 0.1224 > 0.10) and predeclares n >= 150 as a design-time fail-closed feasibility requirement, with deterministic reference tests pinning the arithmetic. The gate remains proposed_unaccepted pending independent review; no locked-run data was used.
  • F5 benchmark expansion (E2/E3): the RF validation suite now includes the oblique-RF adapter (aorsf) when installed, giving the adapter its first F5 FDP evidence, and the start-of-run knockoff probe verifies the 0.2.2 shipped-pair scale contract on a heterogeneous-scale design (column sds 0.01-100) instead of a standardized one.

Audit hotfixes (source audit of 0.2.1, PR #3 follow-up)

  • Fixed-X shipped-pair scale contract completed (flagged behavior change): 0.2.1 rescaled the fixed-X knockoffs to the standardized design but still shipped them next to the caller’s raw matrix — a mismatched pair whenever input columns were heterogeneous. The construction now runs on the raw design (create.fixed normalizes internally, scale only) and the knockoffs are back-transformed by the input column norms, so the shipped pair (x, xk) satisfies the fixed-X Gram condition on the input’s own scale: t(xk) xk = t(x) x exactly and t(x) xk = t(x) x - diag(s) with s_j >= 0. The real block is untouched; the pre-construction centering/scaling step is removed. Gram/cross-Gram identities and paired-block scale matching are now asserted on the actual x_augmented matrix under heterogeneous scales (column sds 0.01-100). Provenance field knockoff_rescaled_to_standardized_scale is replaced by knockoff_rescaled_to_input_scale.
  • Windows CI fixtures: .gitattributes now enforces LF (and marks .rds binary) for the multiview_parity fixtures; the Windows R-CMD-check manifest failures were checkout line-ending conversion, not hash drift.
  • pkgdown index: the stablr-environments vignette and the print.stabl_env_stability topic are indexed; the site builds clean.
  • Oblique-RF tests: a stale probe (measuring create.fixed’s internal unit-norm scale against a sd ~ 1 expectation, and gating a model-X assertion on a fixed-X build check) was removed; the knockoff_equi signal-recovery assertion now runs wherever the knockoff package is installed.
  • 0.2.1 claim corrections: the F5 measurement of empirical FDP 0.665 was for lasso + model-X equicorrelated knockoffs (not fixed-X), and the “invisible to the learner” causal statement is moderated: for the lasso backend, glmnet’s internal standardization moderates the selection-level impact of a scale mismatch. The contract violation remains the reason for the fix; the 0.2.1 notes above are corrected in place.

stablr 0.2.1

Fixed-X knockoff scale and alignment fix (flagged behavior change)

  • Scale contract: knockoff::create.fixed() column-normalizes its input and returns knockoffs on that internal scale (entries ~ 1/√n). The fixed-X path previously paired these knockoffs with the sd-1 standardized design, violating the fixed-X construction contract (the paired blocks lived on different scales). Knockoffs are now rescaled so that t(Xk) Xk = t(X) X holds on the paired scale. (0.2.2 correction: the F5 measurement of empirical FDP 0.665 cited here was for lasso + model-X equicorrelated knockoffs, not fixed-X; and for the lasso backend the selection-level impact of a scale mismatch is moderated by glmnet’s internal standardization — the contract violation, not a measured FDP figure, is the reason for this fix.) Fits using fixed-X knockoffs (artificial_type = "knockoff") may select different features, and FDP+ estimates on such fits change.
  • Column alignment: artificial features are now shipped in aligned order (injected column k is the artificial counterpart of feature k’s selected subset). The previous random column permutation broke the knockoff swap-symmetry in the bootstrap design, because stability scores are accumulated positionally. Applies to the fixed-X and model-X knockoff types; random-permutation nulls are unaffected.
  • Probes and tests: the knockoff sanity probe (tests and F5 benchmark) now probes the shipped contract (rescaled scale + Gram identity) instead of the internal normalized scale; the formerly CI-gated knockoff quality and calibration assertions now run wherever the knockoff package is available. The end-to-end calibration test was redesigned to the bootstrap-valid model-X regime (knockoff_equi) with an explicit lambda grid and powered signals; fixed-X knockoffs under row subsampling remain documented as an invalid combination and are not asserted.

New experimental oblique random-forest learner (plan item D2)

  • base_learner = "oblique_rf" via make_aorsf_adapter() / auto_oblique_threshold_grid() (aorsf backend, negation importance), mirroring the random-forest adapter: importance-threshold penalty path, per-tree seeds drawn from the caller’s seeded RNG stream, and the same model-X-knockoff-pairing guardrail. As with rf, selection frequencies are noisier than the glmnet family’s; the adapter is experimental and FDP+ calibration is empirical (F5-style benchmarks). aorsf is a Suggests dependency; the feature is guarded by .require_pkg().

Multiview-parity fixtures (plan item F4)

  • SHA-256-pinned fixtures (tests/testthat/fixtures/multiview_parity/) lock the vendored cooperative-learning backend’s outputs to CRAN multiview 1.0 on gaussian, binomial, and weighted fits, plus the documented B1/B2/B3 divergence sites (offset handling in build_predmat, warm-start residual weighting, lower.limits clamping). Upstream build_predmat errors with an offset (divergence D4 confirmed live); the vendored fix is pinned by fixture. Makes the PATCHES.cooperative.md divergence log testable.

stablr 0.2.0

Breaking renames ship with deprecation shims that warn for one minor release before removal.

Scientific correctness

  • Behavior change (flagged): the fixed-X knockoff path now standardizes the input matrix before calling knockoff::create.fixed(), matching that function’s documented contract. Fits on heterogeneous feature scales may select different features. Standardization details (means, sds, zero- variance handling) are recorded in the fit provenance, and the fixed-X documentation now states the bootstrap-reuse caveat.
  • FDP+ communication: new “What FDP+ is and is not” vignette section and documented interpretation caveats on get_fdrs().

Vendored cooperative-backend fixes

  • Offset subsetting in build_predmat: the cross-validation prediction path now subsets the offset argument per fold instead of referencing an undefined symbol. The path was previously unreachable because offsets are not exposed through the public API.
  • Halved-step residual weighting: after step-halving, the warm-start residual now weights the offset consistently with the non-halved branch.
  • lower.limits symmetry: the cooperative path now passes lower.limits to elnet.fit() alongside upper.limits.
  • Divergence log: inst/PATCHES.cooperative.md records every deviation from CRAN multiview 1.0.

All backend fixes are inherited from CRAN multiview 1.0 and are behavior-neutral under unit weights, the only weighting stablr exercises today.

API consistency

  • seed deprecated: classic_bootstrap_indices() and group_bootstrap_indices() now take random_state; seed still works but warns, and will be removed in the following minor release. The helpers no longer clobber the global RNG state (withr promoted from Suggests to Imports).
  • Similarity-metric argument renames: adjusted_similarity() and pearson_similarity() (and their _values/_measure variants) rename their arguments to set1/set2/n_universe; old names keep working through deprecation shims.
  • New accessors: get_fdrs() and get_lambda_grid() expose fitted FDP+ estimates and the lambda grid, with documented interpretation caveats.
  • New S3 methods: plot.stabl_fit() and summary.stabl_fit() (with print.summary.stabl_fit()) for fitted STABL objects.
  • Internal: late-fusion internal formals are dot-prefixed so user arguments passed through ... cannot collide with them; no user-visible impact.

New capabilities (extensions beyond Python STABL, labeled experimental)

  • Random-forest base learner: base_learner = "rf" via make_ranger_adapter() and auto_rf_threshold_grid() — permutation- importance threshold paths so the full STABL machinery runs unchanged on non-linear signals. Random forests must be paired with model-X knockoff artificial features; the anti-conservative random-permutation pairing now warns. Calibration is validated empirically by the F5 benchmark (benchmarks/f5_rf_validation.R).
  • Environment-stability workflow: stabl_environment_stability() fits STABL per environment (batch, cohort, site) and aggregates selection frequencies by their minimum across environments — an ICP-inspired transportability heuristic without causal assumptions or new dependencies — with get_min_scores(), a print method, and a new vignette.

Tests and documentation

  • Golden-path rendering tests for all four plotting functions (plot-data correctness: rows, mappings, threshold geometries, FDP+ curve values).
  • Lambda-grid leakage guidance for cross-validated multi-omic workflows, a note on the classification-bootstrap subsample deviation, dead-code removal in the MVR knockoff solver, and the release-evidence glossary moved from the repository root to docs/CONTEXT.md.

stablr 0.1.1

Release correctness

  • Late-fusion weights now default to leakage-safe out-of-fold training. Each stacking fold reruns STABL selection and its downstream learner using only fold-training samples; late_fusion_training = "python_legacy" preserves the historical Python-compatible in-sample algorithm.
  • Named outcomes, groups, bootstrap strata, and validation outcomes are canonically aligned to omic sample identifiers before fusion.
  • OOF provenance records named fold assignments, seeds, selected features, artificial-feature metadata, warnings, fallbacks, and full-refit diagnostics.
  • Scalar stacking now rejects malformed outcomes and infinite observed predictions instead of allowing invalid metric inputs.
  • Binary event levels and multiclass probability columns are now validated explicitly; probability rows must be complete, finite, and normalized, and metric calculations no longer silently discard malformed observations.

Architecture, profiling, and calibration hardening

  • Fixed-X knockoff correctness: fixed-X construction now rejects row- augmented knockoffs and uses the documented random-permutation fallback. Truncating only the knockoff matrix to the original row count violated the fixed-X Gram identities when p < n < 2p; fallback provenance records the reason.
  • FDP+ performance and contracts: threshold counts now sort once per score vector and use interval lookup, preserving strict > tie semantics and first-minimum threshold selection while avoiding feature-by-threshold logical allocations. Public inputs now reject malformed, non-finite, out-of-range, or column-incompatible score matrices.
  • Learner-module depth: public single-lambda glmnet and adaptive-lasso adapters now delegate to the same path-fitting implementations used by the batched bootstrap interface, removing duplicate fitting and coefficient- extraction logic without changing seeded fitted outputs.
  • Methodology runner: artificial-feature strategies are compared on paired simulated data and fit seeds. Replicate artifacts record both seeds, and summaries report SD and Monte Carlo SE for selection count, empirical FDP, and TPR, plus Monte Carlo SE for FDP-exceedance and fallback rates.
  • ROC/PRC diagnostics: plot_roc() and plot_prc() reject ambiguous or incomplete labels and probabilities, and aggregate tied scores so metrics are row-order invariant.
  • Python parity evidence: reproducible Python 3.11 fixtures pin the public STABL reference commit and include frozen matrices, bootstrap schedules, artificial features, lambda grids, masks, FDP+ curves, stacking candidates, solver-ranking contracts, provenance, and a SHA-256 manifest.
  • MVR knockoffs: solver checks now cover PSD feasibility, objective behaviour, determinism, and caller RNG isolation. Fallbacks and approximate high-dimensional chunking carry explicit provenance.
  • Release infrastructure: expanded the R CMD check platform matrix, installed-package methodology runner resolution, always-uploaded check artifacts, one-pass Cobertura/Codecov reporting, release-gated pkgdown deployment, the canonical manual R-hub v2 workflow for sanitizer and specialist-platform checks, GPL and vendored-code provenance, and reproducible bundled OOL data preparation.
  • Metadata and documentation: set the release version to 0.1.1, refreshed the citation and method DOIs, credited the STABL and multiview contributors, recorded the bundled OOL data source and CC0 terms, and replaced “Pure-R” with the accurate “R-native without a Python runtime” description. Documentation now describes FDP+ as a data-dependent diagnostic minimizer, states its assumptions and fallback limitations, and distinguishes frozen- score parity from end-to-end solver ranking parity.
  • Release evidence: added deterministic tests for sample-order invariance, grouped OOF separation, validation-outcome independence, fold perturbations, sequential/parallel agreement, legacy stacking parity, MVR feasibility, and locked statistical release gates. Validation commands, versions, hashes, warnings, profiling limitations, and platform results are recorded in docs/release/0.1.1-validation.md. Locked long-running validators now require a clean Git source tree, record both start and end provenance, and reject evidence if the tracked tree moves during computation.

stablr 0.1.0

Publication-readiness blocker remediation

  • License: corrected License: field from MIT + file LICENSE to GPL (>= 2) and removed the MIT LICENSE file. The vendored cooperative-learning engine under src/glmnetpp/ is derived from glmnet/multiview (GPL-2); the compiled combined work must therefore be GPL. inst/COPYING.cooperative already documented the GPL-2 component.

  • Repository URLs: updated URL: and BugReports: in DESCRIPTION and the package URL in inst/CITATION from the upstream Python repo (gregbellan/Stabl) to the canonical R package repo (mdmanurung/stablr).

  • Contributors: added the original STABL method authors (Hédou, Marić, Bellan, Gfeller — Nat Biotechnol 2024) and the cooperative-learning/multiview authors (Ding, Li, Narasimhan, Tibshirani — PNAS 2022) as ctb in Authors@R, consistent with the already-correct inst/CITATION entries.

  • Cox in late fusion: late_fusion = TRUE with family = "cox" now throws a clear error instead of silently scoring with R-squared and OLS predictors (both invalid for censored data). Early-fusion and per-omic cox remain valid. Mirrors the existing cooperative-fusion cox guard.

  • README: documented the C++17 compiler / toolchain requirement (Rtools on Windows, Xcode CLT on macOS, gcc/clang on Linux) and added a canonical remotes::install_github() install path.

  • Vignettes: added reader-facing eval = FALSE callout blocks to the three heavy vignettes (stablr-multiomic, stablr-tcga, stablr-tcga-nestedcv) explaining that code is illustrative and how to run it.

  • MCC metric: added Matthews Correlation Coefficient (Gorodkin 2004 multiclass formula) to the list returned by .classification_metrics(). MCC is a standard metric for imbalanced classification, complementing the existing accuracy, BER, and macro-F1. Returns 0 for degenerate (all-one-class) predictions.

  • Elastic-net parity disclosure: the Python-parity fixtures for elastic-net models assert signal ranking (which features are selected), not bit-identical coefficients. R and Python elastic-net implementations use different coordinate descent schedules; ranking parity is the appropriate criterion and is explicitly documented in the test file.

  • Verification: mixOmics (Suggests) is used only in TCGA vignettes and is already guarded by requireNamespace() + global eval = FALSE; no change needed.

  • Release metadata: aligned pkgdown URLs, article listings, and the public reference index with the current mdmanurung/stablr repository. Removed the stale Python-parity article link; the Python-to-R mapping now lives in docs/PYTHON_TO_R_MAPPING.md.

  • Parallel tests: the parallel RNG determinism test now probes future::multisession/PSOCK availability and skips with a clear reason in socket-restricted check sandboxes.

  • Release hardening: added shared scalar validators, duplicate sample/feature name guards, effective FDP+ decoy scaling, transform_stabl() for selected feature subsetting, matrixStats-backed row maxima, bundled Python-parity fixture checks, fixed-seed methodology/stacking scripts, validator rollout across workflow/plot/export helpers, and parity-preserving chunked stacked_multi_omic() evaluation for binary/regression tasks. The multiclass stacking path remains scalar by design to preserve probability-normalization parity. ## Quality and publication-readiness sweep

  • Infrastructure: corrected License: field; lowered Depends: R (>= 4.1.0) from 4.4.0; moved package-level doc to R/stablr-package.R; guarded save_stabl_results() against a missing ggplot2 Suggests dep; removed stray Rplots.pdf build artifacts.

  • Documentation: documented all four print.* S3 methods; added @examples to all 54 exported symbols; replaced duplicated @param blocks with @inheritParams stabl_fit; added @seealso cross-links across the metrics family and compute_fdp_plus.

  • Correctness: guarded cooperative lambda-index lookup against float mismatch; fixed integer overflow in .derive_nested_seed for large fold counts; added explicit stop() default to the cooperation type_measure switch; replaced seq(start+1, start+n) with seq_len(n) idiom at all index ranges; added tie-policy comments at every which.min/which.max site.

  • Performance: centralised rowMaxs helper with edge-case fast paths for 0-row and 1-column matrices; eliminated quadratic c(accumulator, chunk) vector growth in three bootstrap helpers; extracted .BOOTSTRAP_COEF_THRESHOLD named constant; halved pairwise-similarity call count in jaccard_matrix, adjusted_similarity_values, and pearson_similarity_values via upper-triangle loops.

  • Internal quality: extracted .require_ggplot2() to replace six identical inline guards; collapsed .cooperative_selected_features two-pass loop to a single lapply; vectorised the finite-check in .multiclass_log_loss; extracted .scores_to_long_df to deduplicate the real- and artificial-feature long-data-frame loops in plot_stabl_path.

  • Tests: added tests for get_stabl_scores and load_ool_data; modernised skip() to skip_if() idiom. Current local no-vignette release check: FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 1 | PASS 1611. No-manual/no-vignette R CMD check is Status: OK; all six source vignettes rendered to /tmp/stablr-vignette-review; pkgdown built to /tmp/stablr-pkgdown.

  • CI: added .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml (ubuntu release+devel, macOS release) with a separate covr/Codecov coverage job; gated heavy vignettes (stablr-multiomic, stablr-tcga, stablr-tcga-nestedcv) with eval = FALSE in their setup chunks.

Native cooperative learning (multiview engine)

  • Vendored CRAN multiview v1.0 cooperative-learning engine (GPL-2 submodule in inst/COPYING.cooperative) for gaussian and binomial cooperative fusion.
  • No runtime dependency on the external multiview package for cooperative workflows.
  • Compiled C++ core (wls_exp, glmnetpp headers) with NeedsCompilation: yes.
  • New vignette("stablr-advanced") documents Cox, knockoffs, grouped bootstrap, reproducibility metrics, export helpers, and outer CV.

Application-note release candidate

  • R-native STABL implementation without a Python runtime, with glmnet backends (lasso, elastic net, adaptive lasso, optional sparse group lasso).
  • FDP+ thresholding with random-permutation and knockoff artificial features.
  • Multi-omic train/validation, outer CV, and nested CV workflows.
  • Early, late, and cooperative fusion integration paths.
  • Bundled Onset of Labor (OOL) tutorial subset in inst/extdata/.
  • Python parity fixtures and vignettes for cross-language validation.
  • Publication reproduction script: inst/analysis/generate_publication_parity_table.R.

Naming

The package is stablr. Cooperative multi-omic fusion is a workflow inside stablr, not a separate package (costablr is not used).
